exit: ms/committed-token at c=16 beats the no-spec control on the same binary, needle x3 in envelope; or an errors entry names the one execution difference that blocks unifying SpecKind

notes.text: Briefed with the plan; first deliverable is an op_timing shape call, because this is the same shape as batched DSpark over quantized KV, rejected twice.
Reuse settled: verify (taps became Option), accept, rollback and snapshot were already generic; the only new code is the batched draft (mtp_forward_level_batch).

Closed by controller. The lever gate's first run was a no-op (no BASELINE_LOG, so any miss count would pass); the real PASS came from a rerun with a nospec baseline arm. That defect is filed separately.

verdict: Accepted with bounds. The batched draft is correct and ships; the speculation is profitable at c<=4 and loses at c>=8. The exit criterion's first arm failed: decode ms/tok at c=16 is +29.3% vs the no-spec control on the same binary (c=1 -17.3%, c=4 -1.3%, c=8 +27.7%, c=32 +39.7%). The second arm is answered by a different quantity than it asked for: the blocker is not an execution difference in SpecKind but the accept rate. Verify sends 3N rows and returns 1+d*a tokens per step, so it pays only while 1+d*a > cost_ratio; measured cost_ratio 1.6 at c=1 and 2.51 at c=32 against 1+2*0.467 = 1.93, which puts the c=32 break-even accept rate at 0.755 vs the measured 0.467. The lever is drafter quality, not the verify kernel. Correctness held throughout: chains engage at every c (~4200, was 0 at c>=4 before the fix), needle 12/12 exact DET, lever gate PASS.

notes.text: tileRL covers Qwen NextN and DSpark with one DraftHead plus a 7-entry name map (spec.py _DRAFT_TOP), 279 lines total against our 4,567 across 7 files.

verdict: Not mergeable: three real execution differences, not naming. (1) DSpark norms after summing tap projections, MTP norms emb and hidden separately before one fc — different forward graphs; (2) DSpark's batched path is pinned to BF16 KV, and the MTP lever's target config is FP8 KV, so a merged path either inherits the BF16 gate or splits the gate per head; (3) DSpark's persistent ctx ring and multi-tap fc have no MTP counterpart, and MTP's per-block fresh KV has no DSpark one. tileRL's one class carries both norm conventions — that is a union, not a merge.

exit: L2 and L3 single-page cold-read p50/p99 measured, stated as a ratio to one decode step; the entry says whether per-page paging of active sequences is allowed

notes.text: Measured: L2 single-page cold read p50 4.17 ms / p99 4.27 ms = 27%/28% of a decode step; L3 NVMe direct p50 24.1 ms / p99 34.5 ms = 158%/227%. L3 cannot sit inside a decode step, so per-page paging of active sequences is not viable on L3; L2 is marginal.

verdict: L2 fault p50 2.31 ms = 15% of a 15.25 ms decode step; L3 NVMe p50 20.85 ms = 137%. Per-page paging of active sequences is dead on L3 and marginal on L2. Page is 21.77 MiB; L2 is non-pinned host DRAM, L3 is O_DIRECT io_uring QD8; budget is 1000/65.56 tok/s, the 2026-08-14 DSv4-Flash-FP8 c=1 DSpark re-anchor. An earlier byte-sum consumer measured the reduction loop rather than the memory system (cold approx warm) and is superseded by the memcpy consumer.
